evals.name: ssh-install-contract
evals.prompt: I want to put this project on a new Ubuntu VPS: SSH root@203.0.113.9 with ~/.ssh/id_ed25519, endpoint vpn.example.com, UDP 51830. I need AWG 3.1 with the internal DNS and the amiunder.vpn page, but I was told to run awg-tool install --version 3.1 --dns 172.29.172.254 --out phone.conf. Check against the current project whether that plan works and give a detailed supported alternative with no new scripts. Do not connect to the VPS and install nothing: I need exact commands, limits and how to verify the result.
evals.expected_output: install --version 3.1 is accepted as working (container awg31-server, MTU 1280), but --dns and --out are rejected, and the internal DNS and pages are explained as the Compose path; TUN, permissions, volumes, the --host versus --endpoint split and a check with a real client are covered.
expectations: Explains that install takes --version 3.1 and sets up the awg31-server container with MTU 1280, while --dns and --out are not implemented and can be silently ignored.

For the internal resolver and the .vpn pages picks Compose with the vaiprog/amnezia-wg-31, amnezia-wg-dns and amnezia-wg-status images and gen --version 3.1, keeps the resolver's cap_add NET_BIND_SERVICE, and does not start the demo client with an empty config.

Keeps the SSH address and the endpoint apart: --host 203.0.113.9, --endpoint vpn.example.com without a port, --listen-port 51830, and in Compose matches the published port with AWG_ENDPOINT vpn.example.com:51830.
Provides NET_ADMIN, /dev/net/tun, forwarding and a kept state volume; does not recommend privileged mode or deleting volumes.
Saves the client config to an owner-only file (awg-tool peer add --out or umask 077) and requires checking the handshake, DNS and amiunder.vpn from a real client, not only healthy.
Does not guess 3.1 flags: knows the 3.1 preset already turns on RandomTrailers and H1-H4 = 1..4, switches take on and off, and DisableCookies is not turned on without a reason.

evals.name: client-issue-and-revoke
evals.prompt: awg-server already runs on the Docker host with AWG 3.1, network 10.99.0.0/24, and the internal DNS and pages from Compose. I want to add alice-phone with all traffic through vpn.example.com:51820 and keep the config only in a closed file. I also need to revoke for good an old unlabelled peer that is written in server.conf, and to know whether another client's lost private key can be recovered. Give exact commands and the order of steps with no new scripts; do not run anything.
evals.expected_output: Issue through awg-tool peer add --out or docker exec awg-peer with AWG_ENDPOINT and AWG_CLIENT_ALLOWED set to both default routes, a protected file, kept state; the 3.1 switches are copied by issuing; the permanent revoke accounts for server.conf; a lost key cannot be recovered.
expectations: Adds alice-phone with docker exec awg-server awg-peer add, AWG_ENDPOINT=vpn.example.com:51820 and AWG_CLIENT_ALLOWED='0.0.0.0/0, ::/0' (or awg-tool peer add --out with the node's environment set), and does not regenerate the shared obfuscation.
Explains that a full tunnel needs both 0.0.0.0/0 and ::/0, since AmneziaVPN ignores its site lists with only one, and IPv6 would go around the tunnel.
Writes the config to a file with umask 077 or --out, without a TTY, and warns about overwriting the only copy.
Checks the persistent state volume and knows that issuing copies the obfuscation block from the server file whole, including 3.1's RandomTrailers and DisableCookies.
For a permanent revoke of the unlabelled peer removes its block from the original server.conf and the live peer by public key, accounting for the restore at start.
Does not promise to recover a lost client private key; suggests revoking it and issuing a new pair, then checking the handshake.

evals.name: dns-status-and-safe-diagnostics
evals.prompt: A split-tunnel client has a fresh handshake, DNS=172.29.172.254 and AllowedIPs=10.99.0.0/24,172.29.172.254/32 (the config was issued long ago). example.com resolves through that DNS, but amiunder.vpn does not open. The laptop has awg-tool 0.4.0, and awg-tool status --server home shows an empty list although the container runs on the VPS. I want to attach awg-dump to an issue and run awg-tool update --local to update the images. Based on the current code suggest safe diagnostics and fixes, with no remote actions and no new scripts.
evals.expected_output: Names the missing route to the page (services network 172.29.172.0/24), explains the empty remote status as the discovery bug before 0.5.0, describes awg-dump honestly (HPK is cut since 0.5.0, labels and addresses stay), does not call update an image installer; no regenerated parameters and no deleted state.
expectations: Gives the pages address 172.29.172.253 and suggests the 172.29.172.0/24 route (as configs issued since 0.5.0 have) or a reissue, keeping the route to DNS.

Explains the empty remote status as the bug before 0.5.0, where remote commands looked at the local container list, and suggests updating the CLI or looking on the VPS directly, not reinstalling the server.

Says that since 0.5.0 awg-dump cuts the header protection key to <set, N bytes>, but an old image's dump holds it whole, and labels, addresses and public keys stay, so a raw dump is not published unchecked.
Explains that update only checks versions and does not download or recreate images, and gives an agreed manual update path that keeps configs and state.
Does not suggest regenerating obfuscation, exposing DNS or HTTP outside, or deleting volumes to fix these symptoms.

evals.name: alternative-root-domains
evals.prompt: I want .geek domains from OpenNIC to open through the tunnel, and everything else to resolve as now. The Compose resolver already runs, and ./dns is mounted at /etc/awg-dns. How do I set this up in this project, and what are the risks? Do not run anything.
evals.expected_output: Suggests forward.d for one zone or chain.conf with default first, explains why the chain moves on, that answers from the chain are not DNSSEC-validated, and that changes apply without a restart.
expectations: Suggests a forward.d file with the geek. zone and OpenNIC resolver addresses, or chain.conf with default on the first line and an OpenNIC resolver second.
Explains that the chain moves on at NXDOMAIN, SERVFAIL, REFUSED, a timeout or a sinkhole answer such as 0.0.0.0 or 127.0.0.1, so ordinary names resolve as before.
Warns that answers from forwarded zones and further down the chain are not DNSSEC-validated, and advises taking current resolver addresses from their own source.
Says the change is picked up without a restart and suggests checking with awg-tool dns and awg-tool dns query from a tunnel client.

evals.name: client-quirks
evals.prompt: My friends use AmneziaVPN. On Windows big sites hang over 3.1 while small ones load, and on Android the 'Direct' site list does nothing. Their configs say AllowedIPs = 0.0.0.0/0 and MTU = 1280. A vpn:// link I made last month says no protocol is installed. What is going on and what should I do? Do not run anything on the server.
evals.expected_output: Names three known client quirks: site lists need both 0.0.0.0/0 and ::/0, AmneziaVPN on Windows can run a larger MTU than the config (clamped by the node's MSS rule since 0.5.1), and vpn:// links from before 0.5.1 need reissuing; suggests awg-tool check on the files and an image update in an agreed window.
expectations: Explains that AmneziaVPN applies its site lists only when AllowedIPs holds both 0.0.0.0/0 and ::/0, on every platform including Android, and that awg-tool check warns about it.

Links the hanging big sites to the client running a larger MTU than the config, and says images from 0.5.1 clamp forwarded TCP MSS on a NAT node (AWG_MSS), so the fix is an image update, not bigger S or J values.
Says vpn:// links built by awg-tool before 0.5.1 use a format AmneziaVPN does not import, and suggests reissuing with 0.5.1 or newer.
Suggests running awg-tool check on the configs where they are, without pasting them into the chat, and asks for agreement before any server change.
